Noah (CS): Heads-up — KiteMetrics onboarding shows p98 latency spikes ~1.3s on ~512-token generates. Renewal flagged as ‘watch’. Recommend a cautious quant-swap + session-aware routing canary to demonstrably reduce tail latency and cost.

Rhea M. (Solutions): Proposed plan: split routing by token_count header. Requests <=600 tokens -> redwood/compact-int4 canary; >600 -> redwood/standard-v1. Enable prefix caching for repeated sessions. Start 6% canary for 48h, then evaluate.

Ethan (ML): Quality guardrails: intent accuracy >= baseline -1.0%, numeric extraction F1 >= baseline -2.0 pts. Eval suite: 30 labeled prompts (mix of tables/numbers/dialogue) + spot manual review. Enable KV-cache warmup and batching: target_batch=6, max_wait_ms=12.

Aisha @KiteMetrics: OK on canary if rollback <=10m and we get an exec-friendly cost vs latency chart. Main ask: minimal changes to scoring pipeline; keep scoring outputs identical format.

canary-bot: Canary queued: account=kitemetrics, percent=6, duration=48h, model=redwood/compact-int4, fallback=redwood/standard-v1, id=cb_7782.

Noah (CS): Runbook summary I'll attach: rollout 6% -> 30% -> full over 7d if checks pass. Rollback triggers = extraction_F1 drop >2 pts OR p99 > baseline*1.4 OR error_rate increase >0.5%. Post-canary deliverable = one-pager with latency deltas, per-token cost change, % routed to compact, and any quality notes. Keep alerts in this thread.
